finding.claim: GET /invoice/<inv_id> has no authentication or ownership check, so any unauthenticated caller can read any invoice (including the customer field) by ID (IDOR).
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP GET with attacker-chosen inv_id path parameter (invoices.py:7)
finding.sink: INVOICES.get(inv_id) then jsonify(inv) returns the full invoice (invoices.py:9-10)

trace.note: Route /invoice/<inv_id> registered with no auth decorator
get_invoice(inv_id) takes the path param directly
Dict lookup by attacker-supplied ID; no caller/ownership check
jsonify returns the whole invoice record to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No before_request hook, no auth decorator, no g.user check on this route in invoices.py (grep for before_request/g.user/login_required found only lines 16 and 23). Sibling /my/invoice/<id> enforces ownership at line 16, this route does not. Caveat: an auth middleware outside this file would change the result; none is visible in the repo.

verdict.guard_found: none. invoices.py:7 is a bare @app.route with no auth decorator, and the only before_request/g.user/login_required hits in the repo are the ownership check at invoices.py:16 and the list query at invoices.py:23, both in other routes. The /invoice/<inv_id> handler at lines 8-10 does a dict lookup and returns jsonify(inv) with no ownership check.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: invoices.py:7-10 registers an unauthenticated route that returns any INVOICES entry by ID, and the sibling /my/invoice/<id> ownership check at invoices.py:16 is absent here, so an anonymous caller can read any invoice. The only caveat is that auth middleware outside this repo could block it, and none is visible in the code provided.
